messages.subject: [statnet_help] 64-bit arch install?
messages.body_plain:
Hi list - I'm having memory allocation errors on a 32-bit architecture  
(on a Mac OSX - Leopard).  Not sure why that is as I have 4gb RAM and  
I am getting the "Error: Cannot allocate vector of length xxxx" where  
xxxx is 200mb.  Unfortunately, I can't seem to figure out how to up my  
memory allocation as the R options that are standard on a PC platform  
do not do anything on a Mac OS.  So, first, I guess I should ask if  
anyone else uses a Mac and if they know of a solution to this. Second,  
because of the memory issues, I installed the 64-bit version of R  
along with a Mac GUI to run the 64-bit version.  Does well, runs fast,  
the only problem is, I can't load statnet, getting the message that  
statnet is only for a 32-bit architecture.  So, one way gets me the  
package I need without the memory.  The other gets me the memory  
without the package.  Any suggestions or workarounds would be much  
appreciated.

Thanks,
Ned

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Epidemic Modelling
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was wondering if this list could help me with a couple of questions
related to some work I am doing with the aim of modelling infectious
disease. While I'm new to both R and statnet, I would much rather
contribute to an existing (particularly open-source) project than write
things from scratch.

1) I would like to generate undirected networks with a certain number of
nodes, edges, triangles, 4-loops and other 4-motifs. Most of the statnet
documentation assumes that there is a comparator 'real' dataset, but is
there a simple way to construct networks a priori? (Data on
epidemiological rather than social connections is less often a detailed
study of a small group and more often population-level measurements or
inference on local structure.)

2) Assuming that model terms for the full family of undirected
four-motifs is not already being coded by somebody, does anyone have any
quick hints on how to start contributing? I've downloaded ergmuserterms
and I'm proficient in C but as I said above, am new to R so it's not
that easy for me to understand that package just from the download.

Thanks in advance,
Thomas.


=====================================================================
Department of Biological Sciences (and Warwick Mathematics Institute)
University of Warwick, Coventry, CV4 7AL.       Tel: +44 24 7652 8368
www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/bio/res/populations/riginfo/people/thomas/

messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas.  I've written some comments below.  I apologize in advance  
that they're a bit on the vague side.

On Feb 5, 2009, at 1:28 PM, Thomas House wrote:

> Hello,
>
> I was wondering if this list could help me with a couple of questions
> related to some work I am doing with the aim of modelling infectious
> disease. While I'm new to both R and statnet, I would much rather
> contribute to an existing (particularly open-source) project than  
> write
> things from scratch.
>

Hear, hear! :)

> 1) I would like to generate undirected networks with a certain  
> number of
> nodes, edges, triangles, 4-loops and other 4-motifs. Most of the  
> statnet
> documentation assumes that there is a comparator 'real' dataset, but  
> is
> there a simple way to construct networks a priori? (Data on
> epidemiological rather than social connections is less often a  
> detailed
> study of a small group and more often population-level measurements or
> inference on local structure.)
>

I think that the answer is no -- there is not an easy way to do this  
and in general (i.e., for general types of motifs that you'd like to  
see) I think this is a research-level question -- though perhaps  
someone else on the list can supply a more complete answer.

> 2) Assuming that model terms for the full family of undirected
> four-motifs is not already being coded by somebody, does anyone have  
> any
> quick hints on how to start contributing? I've downloaded  
> ergmuserterms
> and I'm proficient in C but as I said above, am new to R so it's not
> that easy for me to understand that package just from the download.
>

I am not aware of anyone, at least in our group, who has coded the  
four-motifs.

The best thing to do at present is to do exactly what you have done,  
namely download ergmuserterms.  You should also take a look at the  
code in that package, particularly in the files InitErgmTerm.users.R  
(see the comments at the top) and changestats.h.  However, in the not- 
too-distant future there will be better documentation on this, and I  
must apologize personally that said documentation does not already  
exist!  (It's on the to-do list...)

Hope this helps a bit,
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

 

I've got some problems handling network objects. 

 

I've created a bunch of network objects with a vertex attribute. What I
would like to do now for each network is selecting a subgraph based on the
vertex attribute value and then finding the largest component in the
resulting subgraph. In the end, I am interested in each network's largest
component whose nodes were preselected to fulfill certain criteria. 

 

Many thanks in advance,

Torsten
